Original white → white (step 1) → white (step 2) → gray (step 3)? Wait, step 3 turns white into gray, so original white becomes gray. Original black becomes white in step 1, then becomes gray in step 3. Original gray becomes black in step 2, stays black in step 3.

At that point, whites include original whites and former blacks. So both become gray. Grays become black in step 2, and step 3 doesn't affect black.
